novel_features.name: Trend Snapshot
novel_features.description: Quantify what's rising and falling in award-winning design: tag, color-family, and tech frequency over a time window, with window-over-window deltas.
novel_features.rationale: Awwwards has no aggregate view at all; frequency counts and time-window comparisons only exist because the local mirror persists every card.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when you need current design-language evidence ("is dark mode still dominant?") instead of training-data taste. Prerequisite: run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --pages 10' first (add --details for the color axis).

novel_features.name: Design Context Pack
novel_features.description: One-shot design briefing for a build: top-scoring reference sites, dominant palettes, recurring tech, co-occurring style tags, and jury-score benchmarks for a category or style.
novel_features.rationale: Synthesizes five data families (cards, scores, palettes, tags, benchmarks) that no single Awwwards page contains, shaped for direct agent consumption.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this first when designing a site: it turns "what does great look like for this kind of page" into machine-readable input. Prerequisite: run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --pages 10 --details' first; palettes and score benchmarks come from detail data.

novel_features.name: Fuzzy Palette Match
novel_features.description: Find award-winning sites whose palette contains a color near a target hex, ranked by RGB distance.
novel_features.rationale: The site's color filter is exact-hex only over ~30 buckets; nearest-color search needs the extracted palette rows in the local mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a brand color is fixed and you need proof of how top-rated designs deploy colors like it. Prerequisite: palette rows come from detail pages - run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --details' first.

novel_features.name: Ranked Elements
novel_features.description: Section-level inspiration ranked by quality: heroes, footers, or 404 pages from sites whose jury score clears your bar.
novel_features.rationale: The /elements/ wall is flat and unranked; joining sections to parent-site jury scores is a local SQLite join the site cannot do.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before building a specific page section: it returns only the sections from provably high-scoring sites. Prerequisite: run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --elements <type> --details' first.

novel_features.name: Studio Profile
novel_features.description: Aggregated award profile of one agency or studio: wins by tier, average dimension scores, and dominant tags and tech.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a credits-keyed join across websites and directory tables that exists only in the local mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to study how a specific top studio wins: their score profile and signature techniques in one call. Prerequisite: credits come from detail pages - run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --details' first.

narrative.headline: Query Awwwards jury scores, palettes, and tech stacks from a local SQLite mirror - multi-filter search, trend deltas, and one-shot design briefings the site itself can't do.
narrative.value_prop: Awwwards jury-scores the best web design in the world, but that intelligence is locked in server-rendered HTML with one-filter-at-a-time browsing. This CLI mirrors cards, scores, palettes, and tags into local SQLite, then answers questions the site cannot: multi-filter intersections via 'find', trend deltas via 'trends', and one-shot agent design briefings via 'context-pack'.

quickstart.comment: Sanity-check the CLI plumbing (drop --dry-run to also probe awwwards.com)
Today's newest award entries with tags, dates, and thumbnail URLs
Mirror recent winners plus jury scores and palettes into local SQLite - powers every analytics command
Multi-filter AND intersection the site itself cannot do (one filter at a time server-side)
Deep-dive one winner: jury scores by dimension, color palette, tech stack
One-shot design briefing: reference sites + palettes + tech + score benchmarks

troubleshoots.symptom: Analytics commands (trends, context-pack, palette-match) return empty results
troubleshoots.fix: Run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --pages 10 --details' first - these commands read the local design mirror, not the live site

troubleshoots.symptom: HTTP 429 or slow responses during mirror
troubleshoots.fix: Lower the page count ('mirror --pages 3') and re-run later; the built-in rate limiter backs off automatically
Tags are exact strings from Awwwards cards (e.g. 'Three.js', 'GSAP', 'Clean'); run 'awwwards-pp-cli trends --by tag' to see the live tag vocabulary

troubleshoots.symptom: 'sites get <slug>' returns page metadata but you expected scores
troubleshoots.fix: Generated endpoint commands return raw page data; use 'inspect <slug>' for parsed scores, jury votes, and palette

troubleshoots.symptom: elements-top returns items but none ranked, or all unjoined
troubleshoots.fix: Elements rank against their parent site's scores, which come from detail pages. Feed both first: run 'awwwards-pp-cli mirror --elements hero --details'

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI whenever an agent or designer needs grounded evidence about what award-winning web design actually looks like: assembling reference sets for a brief, checking current tag/color/tech trends, benchmarking a design direction against jury scores, or pulling palettes and section-level patterns before writing any CSS. It is the right tool when the question starts with "what does great look like for...".
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to submit sites, vote, or manage an Awwwards account - authenticated features are out of scope
Do not use it to capture full-page screenshots of live sites - it returns Awwwards' own thumbnails and data, not a rendering engine
Do not use it for bulk archival scraping of awwwards.com - it is an interactive tool with conservative rate limits
Do not use it for general web search or non-design research; its universe is Awwwards award entries
